docs.title: 3.2 Entity definitions
docs.text: Entity Purpose Write profile Read profile User Identity and credentials Low High point lookup AuthSession Login/session lifecycle Medium High, TTL-oriented Conversation Chat aggregate and ownership Low/medium High list and detail Message Ordered chat content High append High ordered range AgentDefinition Versioned agent metadata/configuration Low High cached lookup AgentRun Durable execution lifecycle High state transitions High status/detail RunStep Execution trace High append Medium debugging ToolCall Security/audit trace High append Medium audit/detail Memory Long-term/semantic context Medium/high High retrieval OutboxEvent Reliable event publication High append/update Worker polling Artifact Large binary/text output Medium Low direct, high download SensorSample Operational telemetry Very high Aggregated dashboards

docs.title: 3.3 Relational schema rules
docs.text:
• Use UUID identifiers and UTC timestamps.
  • Add foreign keys and unique constraints.
  • Use jsonb for extensible configuration and provider-specific payloads, not for fields needed in frequent filters.
  • Use (conversation_id, sequence_no) as the message ordering key.
  • Use optimistic state transitions for runs: queued -> running -> succeeded|failed|cancelled.
  • Add ownership predicates to every repository query.
  • Use cursor pagination instead of large offset pagination.
  • Store hashes of session tokens, never raw tokens.

Recommended indexes:

CREATE INDEX messages_conversation_seq
  ON messages (conversation_id, sequence_no DESC);

CREATE INDEX conversations_user_updated
  ON conversations (user_id, updated_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX runs_status_created
  ON agent_runs (status, created_at);

CREATE INDEX runs_conversation_created
  ON agent_runs (conversation_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE INDEX memories_scope_created
  ON memories (user_id, agent_id, created_at DESC);

docs.title: 3.4 Database selection by use case
docs.text: Use case Local deployment Production/multi-process deployment Reason Users, auth, conversations, messages SQLite WAL PostgreSQL ACID transactions and ownership constraints Agent definitions SQLite PostgreSQL Versioning and reliable configuration Runs, steps, tool calls SQLite single writer PostgreSQL Durable recovery and concurrent workers Sessions, locks, rate limits SQLite/session table Redis plus durable session record TTL and atomic coordination Semantic memory SQLite metadata + optional file index PostgreSQL + pgvector Relational filters plus vector search Event delivery In-process event bus PostgreSQL outbox + Redis Streams/broker Reliable cross-process delivery Large artifacts Local filesystem S3-compatible object storage Avoid oversized transactional rows Sensor metrics In-memory bounded metrics Prometheus/TimescaleDB/ClickHouse High write rate and retention

docs.title: 3.5 Database decision
docs.text:
The recommended sequence is:

  1. Implement repository ports and migrations.
  2. Support SQLite for single-user/local mode.
  3. Add PostgreSQL as the production system of record.
  4. Add Redis only for ephemeral state, distributed locks, live streams, and rate limits.
  5. Add pgvector before adopting a dedicated vector database.
  6. Add a time-series or columnar database only when sensor/event volume justifies its operational cost.

Do not use Redis as the source of truth for conversations or runs. Do not put high-frequency sensor samples in message tables. Do not introduce MongoDB merely because message payloads contain JSON; the core entities have strong relationships, ownership, ordering, and transactional state transitions.

docs.title: 4.1 API conventions
docs.text:
• Base path: /api/v1
  • JSON request/response bodies.
  • UUIDs in canonical string form.
  • UTC ISO-8601 timestamps.
  • Authorization: Bearer <token> for API clients; signed browser sessions may remain as a local UI adapter.
  • Idempotency-Key required for message creation and other retriable commands.
  • Cursor pagination: ?limit=50&after=<cursor>.
  • Return 202 Accepted for asynchronous agent work.
  • Use X-Correlation-ID when provided, otherwise generate one.

Standard error:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "conversation_not_found",
    "message": "Conversation does not exist",
    "correlation_id": "uuid"
  }
}

Method Endpoint Purpose GET /health Liveness/readiness and dependency status GET /metrics Runtime and application metrics GET /events/stream Authenticated operational event stream GET /orchestration Agent registry/scheduler status

The existing /chat endpoint can remain temporarily as a compatibility adapter. It should internally create a conversation message and run, then wait for the run only when a legacy client requires a synchronous response.

docs.title: 4.6 Chat request sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as Chat API
    participant DB as SQL Database
    participant O as Outbox Publisher
    participant W as Agent Worker
    participant L as LLM/Tools

    C->>API: POST conversation message + Idempotency-Key
    API->>DB: Transaction: append message, create run, append outbox

    W->>L: Think/plan/LLM/tool calls

    W->>DB: Persist steps, tool calls, assistant message, run result
    W-->>C: Stream/poll shows agent.response.created

docs.title: 5.2 HLD boundaries
docs.text:
1. API adapter validates HTTP input and maps errors. It does not execute long-running agent work.
  2. Application services implement use cases and transaction boundaries.
  3. Domain layer owns entity rules, state transitions, and authorization policies.
  4. Ports define stable interfaces for persistence, events, LLMs, tools, memory, and artifacts.
  5. Kernel/runtime continues to provide event dispatch, routing, scheduling, context, sensors, and agent lifecycle.
  6. Infrastructure adapters select SQLite/PostgreSQL, Redis, vector, object, and metrics implementations at composition time.

docs.title: Local mode
docs.text:
FastAPI + Kernel + Agent Worker
             |
       SQLite WAL + filesystem

Suitable for one user or one local process. Use one database writer and bounded in-process queues.

docs.title: Production mode
docs.text:
API replicas -> PostgreSQL
Worker replicas -> PostgreSQL
             -> Redis (locks, streams, TTL)
             -> Object storage

The PostgreSQL outbox is the reliable source for domain events. Redis improves latency but is not the source of truth.

docs.title: 6.3 Ports and interfaces
docs.text:
class ConversationRepository(Protocol):
    async def get_owned(self, conversation_id: str, user_id: str): ...
    async def create(self, user_id: str, title: str | None): ...


class MessageRepository(Protocol):
    async def append(self, message): ...
    async def list_context(self, conversation_id: str, limit: int): ...


class RunRepository(Protocol):
    async def create(self, command): ...
    async def claim(self, run_id: str, worker_id: str): ...
    async def transition(self, run_id: str, expected, target, patch): ...


class EventPublisher(Protocol):
    async def publish(self, event): ...


class MemoryStore(Protocol):
    async def store(self, item): ...
    async def retrieve(self, query, scope, limit): ...
    async def delete(self, memory_id, scope): ...

Concrete implementations must raise an explicit configuration or infrastructure error when unavailable. They must not silently return a dummy ID, empty result, or success-shaped fallback.

docs.title: Message submission transaction
docs.text:
BEGIN
  verify conversation ownership
  verify Idempotency-Key has not already succeeded
  allocate message sequence_no
  INSERT messages(user message)
  INSERT agent_runs(status = queued)
  INSERT outbox_events(chat.message.created)
  INSERT outbox_events(agent.run.queued)
COMMIT

docs.title: Worker claim
docs.text:
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status = 'running', started_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, worker_id = :worker
WHERE id = :run_id
  AND status = 'queued'
RETURNING *;

If no row is returned, another worker claimed the run or it is no longer eligible. This prevents duplicate execution.

docs.title: Run completion transaction
docs.text:
BEGIN
  INSERT run_steps and tool_calls
  INSERT assistant message with next sequence_no
  UPDATE agent_runs SET status = succeeded, output = ...
  INSERT outbox_events(agent.response.created)
COMMIT

docs.title: 6.5 State machines
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued
    queued --> running: worker claims
    running --> succeeded: output committed
    running --> failed: non-retryable error
    running --> cancelled: cancellation accepted
    running --> queued: retryable failure
    failed --> queued: explicit retry
    succeeded --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

Agent instance lifecycle remains compatible with the current implementation:

INITIALIZED -> READY -> RUNNING -> READY
                         |          |
                         v          v
                       FAILED    TERMINATED

docs.title: 6.6 Event contract
docs.text:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "type": "agent.response.created",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "source": "run-worker",
  "aggregate_type": "agent_run",
  "aggregate_id": "uuid",
  "actor_id": "uuid",
  "correlation_id": "uuid",
  "causation_id": "uuid",
  "occurred_at": "2026-10-20T19:45:00Z",
  "data": {
    "conversation_id": "uuid",
    "message_id": "uuid"
  }
}

Consumers use event.id for idempotency. Commands such as chat.send_message must not be confused with facts such as chat.message.created.

docs.title: 6.7 Context and memory algorithm
docs.text:
1. Load the last N messages using conversation_id and sequence_no.
2. Load relevant long-term memories using user/agent/conversation scope.
3. Apply expiry, deletion, permission, and retention filters.
4. If semantic search is enabled, pre-filter metadata, then retrieve top-k.
5. Apply token budget and summarize older context if necessary.
6. Produce an immutable `TaskRequest.context` for the agent's `execute` call.

docs.title: 6.8 Error handling and retries
docs.text:
• Validation errors return 400.
  • Authentication failures return 401.
  • Ownership/permission failures return 403 or 404 without leaking existence.
  • Duplicate idempotency keys return the original result.
  • Transient LLM, database, or broker failures use bounded exponential retry.
  • Tool failures are recorded in tool_calls and are visible to the agent.
  • Unrecoverable runs become failed with a sanitized error code.
  • Outbox failures retry and eventually enter a dead-letter state.
  • No broad exception handler may convert failure into an empty response.

docs.title: 6.9 Migration plan
docs.text:
1. Add migrations and a database configuration adapter; stop initializing tables from the API request path.
  2. Introduce repository ports and a SQLite adapter.
  3. Persist conversations, messages, runs, steps, and tool calls.
  4. Replace ChatAgent._conversation_histories with repository-backed context.
  5. Implement a real SQLite memory store and remove the dummy memory fallback.
  6. Add PostgreSQL adapters and an outbox publisher.
  7. Move agent execution into a worker entry point.
  8. Add Redis for distributed locks, TTL state, and response streams.
  9. Add pgvector, object storage, and time-series storage only when measured workload requires them.

docs.title: 6.10 Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
The design is complete when:

  • Restarting VIRA does not lose users, conversations, messages, or completed runs.
  • Two users cannot access each other's data.
  • Retried requests do not create duplicate messages or runs.
  • A crashed worker leaves a recoverable run.
  • Every tool call has a durable permission decision and outcome.
  • Memory retrieval returns persisted, correctly scoped records.
  • SQLite works for local single-writer mode.
  • PostgreSQL supports separate API and worker processes.
  • Event consumers safely handle duplicate delivery.

docs.title: Tool Search and Prompt Budgeting
docs.text:
VIRA must not put every tool into every prompt. The current implementation:

  1. builds a ToolCatalog from tool name, description, schema, category and tags;
  2. ranks tools for the user's message;
  3. gives the model a small relevant set plus tool_search;
  4. expands the model's tool set only when it calls tool_search;
  5. rebuilds the prompt with the expanded set on the next step.

Examples:

  • photoshop → tools tagged adobe/photoshop
  • davinci resolve → tools tagged davinci-resolve/media
  • device usage focus → insights
  • web news → web search/research/browse tools

The MCP server also exposes search_tools with its own catalogue so standalone MCP clients can avoid loading every tool.

docs.title: Current scoring
docs.text:
• phrase in tool name
  • exact tag/token matches
  • name token matches
  • description token matches
  • category match
  • fallback to core web/workspace/runtime/insights tools

docs.title: Future algorithm
docs.text:
Replace the keyword ranker with a two-stage retriever:

  1. Candidate retrieval
  2. embeddings over tool name + description + app/domain tags
  3. hierarchical namespaces (adobe/photoshop, blackmagic/davinci, web)
  4. synonym and app-alias expansion
  5. Re-ranking
  6. usage feedback (which tools succeeded for similar tasks)
  7. tool cost/latency estimate
  8. required-argument similarity
  9. user/agent permission filter
  10. category diversity
  11. Prompt budgeter
  12. hard cap on tool count and rendered description chars
  13. collapse tools into compact one-line specs
  14. keep a tool_search / tool_describe meta-tool
  15. only include full schemas for the final shortlist
  16. Learning loop
  17. store (query, selected tools, tool call outcome)
  18. periodically rebuild app/domain bundles
  19. evaluate retrieval recall on a golden task set

The interfaces are already separated (ToolCatalog.search/select, AgentLoop dynamic expansion), so a vector or hybrid retriever can replace the scorer without changing agents or the MCP wire contract.

docs.title: VIRA Family Client — System Design
docs.text:
Status: Draft v0.1 · Audience: Flutter and VIRA-server developers · Scope: the cross-platform client app (Android, iOS/iPadOS, Linux, web) for the Private Family Assistant use case, and the server additions it requires.

Companion to SYSTEM_DESIGN.md (server) and MULTI_DEVICE_IMPLEMENTATION.md. This document is written so a developer can start coding from it: every requirement has an ID, every API has a payload, every table has DDL, and the client internals are specified down to class level.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Purpose, scope and conventions
  2. Functional requirements
  3. Non-functional requirements
  4. High-level design (HLD)
  5. Entities and domain model
  6. Database schema
  7. API design
  8. Low-level design (LLD)
  9. Security and privacy design
  10. Testing strategy
  11. Delivery plan
  12. Risks and open questions
  13. Requirement traceability

docs.title: 1.1 Purpose
docs.text:
The VIRA server (a family PC, mini-server or Raspberry Pi) is a private, local-first AI runtime. The Family Client is the app each family member installs on their phone, tablet or laptop. It lets a household:

  • keep notes, checklists and shared lists that sync between members,
  • get reminders and notifications,
  • chat with VIRA, grounded in the household's own notes,
  • do all of this offline-first and at zero running cost to the user (the family owns the server; no paid cloud is required).

docs.title: 1.2 Goals and non-goals
docs.text: Goals Non-goals (v1) Fully usable offline; sync is background work Real-time co-editing of one note (no CRDT) One codebase for Android, iOS, iPadOS, Linux, web Public cloud-hosted VIRA ("VIRA Cloud") Free connectivity paths (LAN, free VPN/tunnel) End-to-end encryption between members (see §9.6, planned) Minimal data capture; everything opt-in and visible Screen, keystroke or contact harvesting Hindi + English from day one; i18n-ready Calendar/e-mail integrations (v2) Small, understandable server additions Replacing the existing VIRA web dashboard

docs.title: 1.3 Personas
docs.text: Persona Needs Typical device Household admin (e.g. parent who runs the server) Add/remove members, set roles, see server status Laptop + phone Adult member Notes, lists, reminders, chat Android/iOS phone Child member Limited sharing, safe chat, reminders assigned to them Low-end Android phone/tablet Guest View one shared notebook/list Browser (web client)

docs.title: 1.4 Conventions used in this document
docs.text:
• Requirement priority: Must / Should / Could. Release: v1 (MVP) or v2.
  • API status tags: [EXISTING] already in the VIRA server, [EXTEND] exists but needs change, [NEW] must be built.
  • Identifiers: all new entities use client-generatable UUIDv7 strings (time-ordered), so records can be created offline. Users keep their existing public_id.
  • Timestamps: UTC, ISO-8601 with Z in JSON; stored as TEXT ISO-8601 on the server and as epoch milliseconds (INTEGER) in the client DB.
  • Base path: /api/v1. Errors use the existing envelope { "detail": "...", "error": { "code", "message", "correlation_id" } }.
  • Code samples are Dart 3 / Flutter 3.x and Python 3.11 / FastAPI, matching the existing code base. Package names are suggestions; verify current versions before pinning.

docs.title: 1.5 What the current server already gives us
docs.text: Capability Existing endpoint / module Use in client Device enrollment, hashed credentials shown once POST /api/v1/devices Pairing Device heartbeat POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/heartbeat Presence, version reporting Per-user filtered SSE GET /api/v1/stream Realtime "something changed" hints Streaming chat (NDJSON) POST /chat/stream VIRA chat UI Conversations / messages with Idempotency-Key /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages Chat history Scoped memories /memories Grounding for chat Typed principals, audit log, user admin auth/*, /api/v1/admin/* Roles, audit Correlation IDs, cursor pagination api/deps.py All new APIs

docs.title: 1.6 What is missing (drives the server work in §7.10)
docs.text:
1. No household / family concept (access is per device, not per content).
  2. No notes, checklists, reminders entities and no sync protocol.
  3. Mobile auth is cookie-based; device credentials only carry scopes events:write and heartbeat.
  4. No attachment upload/download API.
  5. No push notification path.
  6. The event allow-list rejects user.* / agent.* events by design, so note content must not travel as events.

docs.title: 2.1 Onboarding, pairing and session
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-01 The app opens a setup screen on first launch with two choices: "Join my family's VIRA" (scan QR / enter code) and "Set up a new server" (instructions + link). Must v1 CFR-02 A user can pair by scanning a QR code or typing a short pairing code plus a server address. Must v1 CFR-03 Pairing registers the phone as a device owned by the user and stores its credential only in OS secure storage. Must v1 CFR-04 The QR payload contains one or more server endpoints, the server TLS certificate fingerprint, a one-time code and a protocol version; the app validates all of them before connecting. Must v1 CFR-05 The app keeps the user signed in using short-lived access tokens plus a rotating refresh token; the user never retypes a password on the phone. Must v1 CFR-06 A user can view the devices they have paired, rename them and revoke any of them (including the current one). Should v1 CFR-07 If the server revokes the device or user, the app locks, offers "export my local notes", then wipes server-derived data on confirmation. Must v1 CFR-08 App-lock (biometric/PIN) can be enabled per device. Should v1

docs.title: 2.2 Households and members
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-10 A user belongs to one or more households; the UI shows one active household at a time with a switcher. Must v1 CFR-11 Roles are admin, adult, child, guest. The role matrix in §9.3 is enforced by the server and mirrored in the UI (hidden/disabled actions). Must v1 CFR-12 An admin can generate a pairing code for a new member with a chosen role and expiry (default 15 min, single use). Must v1 CFR-13 An admin can change a member's role or remove the member. Removal purges that member's local copy on their next sync. Must v1 CFR-14 Members see who else is in the household and who last edited a shared item. Should v1 CFR-15 A member can leave a household. Should v1

docs.title: 2.3 Notes and notebooks
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-20 Create, edit, pin, archive, delete and restore (30-day trash) notes while offline. Must v1 CFR-21 Notes live in notebooks. Each notebook has visibility private, household or custom (shared with named members, each view or edit). Must v1 CFR-22 Note body is lightweight Markdown (headings, bold/italic, lists, links). Max 100 KB. Must v1 CFR-23 Tags, colour and pin; list sorted by pinned then last-edited. Should v1 CFR-24 Full-text search across all locally available notes, offline. Must v1 CFR-25 Show "last edited by X on device Y" and a version indicator for shared notes. Should v1 CFR-26 When a conflicting edit is detected the app keeps both: the server version stays, the local version becomes a visible conflict copy the user can merge or delete. Must v1 CFR-27 Export a notebook as Markdown/ZIP. Could v2

docs.title: 2.4 Checklists and shared lists
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-30 A note can be of kind checklist. Items are independent rows (add, edit, reorder, check, delete). Must v1 CFR-31 Two members editing different items of the same list never conflict. Must v1 CFR-32 Items can be assigned to a member. "Assigned to me" is a filtered view. Should v1 CFR-33 Checked items move to a collapsible "Done" section; "clear done" is one tap. Should v1 CFR-34 Pre-built templates: Groceries, Packing, Chores. Could v1

docs.title: 2.5 Reminders
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-40 Create reminders with title, due date/time, time zone and optional repeat rule (daily/weekly/monthly/custom RRULE). Must v1 CFR-41 A reminder is assigned to one member or to "everyone". Each assignee completes it independently. Must v1 CFR-42 Reminders fire as local notifications scheduled on the device, so they work offline and with no server. Must v1 CFR-43 Snooze (10 min / 1 h / tomorrow) and "mark done" actions directly from the notification. Must v1 CFR-44 A reminder can link to a note or list item. Should v1 CFR-45 Reminders are rescheduled after device reboot, time-zone change and app update. Must v1

docs.title: 2.6 Attachments
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-50 Attach photos, PDFs and voice notes to a note. Default max 25 MB (server-configurable, never above the tunnel limit advertised by the server). Must v2 CFR-51 Uploads are resumable, run in the background and are retried; downloads are lazy and cached with an LRU limit. Must v2 CFR-52 Thumbnails are generated on the device before upload. Should v2 CFR-53 Scan a paper document to PDF with on-device edge detection. Could v2

docs.title: 2.7 Sync and offline
docs.text: ID Requirement Priority Rel. CFR-60 All reads come from the local database; all writes go to the local database first and into a durable outbox. Must v1 CFR-61 Sync is triggered by: app foreground, local change (debounced), server hint (SSE or push), connectivity regained, and a periodic background job. Must v1 CFR-62 Every pushed operation carries a client-generated op_id; retries are idempotent. Must v1 CFR-63 Pull is cursor-based and resumable; the client can recover from an expired/compacted cursor by re-bootstrapping. Must v1 CFR-64 The UI always shows sync state per item (synced / pending / conflict / failed) and globally (online, offline, syncing). Must v1 CFR-65 Losing access to a notebook removes its content from the device on the next sync (forget change). Must v1

docs.title: 3. Non-functional requirements
docs.text: ID Category Requirement / target CNFR-01 Offline 100% of read and write features in §2.3–2.5 work with no network. CNFR-02 Startup Cold start to first interactive frame ≤ 2.0 s on a 3 GB RAM / mid-range Android device; ≤ 1.0 s warm. CNFR-03 Responsiveness Local queries ≤ 50 ms p95 for 10 000 notes; scrolling at 60 fps (no jank > 16 ms in lists of 1 000 items). CNFR-04 Sync latency Change visible on another online member's device ≤ 3 s on LAN, ≤ 10 s over VPN/tunnel, when SSE or push is available. CNFR-05 Sync efficiency Idle app generates no network traffic other than the SSE/long-poll connection and heartbeat (≤ 1 per 5 min). Pull of 100 changes ≤ 100 KB. CNFR-06 Battery No foreground service. Background work only via OS-scheduled jobs (≥ 15 min period) and push wake-ups. CNFR-07 Size Android APK/AAB download ≤ 40 MB (arm64 split); iOS ≤ 60 MB. CNFR-08 Platforms Android 8.0+ (API 26), iOS/iPadOS 15+, Linux (x64, GTK/Wayland and X11), evergreen browsers (Chromium, Firefox, Safari 16+). CNFR-09 Reliability No acknowledged local write is ever lost: durable outbox survives crash, kill and reboot. Sync is at-least-once with idempotent apply (effectively exactly-once). CNFR-10 Consistency Eventual consistency; all replicas converge after quiescence. Per-entity versions are monotonic. CNFR-11 Security TLS or WireGuard on every non-LAN hop; certificate pinning on LAN HTTPS; secrets only in Keychain/Keystore; local DB encrypted (SQLCipher) on mobile/desktop. CNFR-12 Privacy Data minimisation per §2.10; no third-party SDKs that collect analytics; push payloads contain no user content. CNFR-13 Observability Every API call carries X-Correlation-ID; client keeps a 2 MB redacted ring-buffer log; sync status is inspectable in the diagnostics screen. CNFR-14 Compatibility Client sends X-Vira-Client: flutter/<semver> proto/<int>. Server supports the current and previous protocol version; older clients get a clear "update required" screen. CNFR-15 Limits Note body ≤ 100 KB; ≤ 200 ops per push; ≤ 500 changes per pull page; household ≤ 12 members; attachment ≤ 25 MB default. CNFR-16 Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA; all interactive elements labelled for screen readers. CNFR-17 Testability ≥ 80% line coverage on domain/ and data/sync/; deterministic clock and ID generator injectable everywhere. CNFR-18 Maintainability Feature-first layered architecture (§8.1); no feature imports another feature's presentation/ code; lints enforced in CI. CNFR-19 Cost Zero mandatory recurring cost for the family. Any shared service (push gateway) must run within free tiers at the target scale of a few thousand households. CNFR-20 Upgradability Local DB migrations are forward-only, tested from every released schema version; a failed migration never deletes user data (backup copy first).

docs.title: 4.1 System context
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Family["Family devices (Flutter app)"]
        A1["Phone (Android/iOS)"]
        A2["Tablet / iPad"]
        A3["Laptop (Linux)"]
        A4["Browser (web)"]
    end

    subgraph Home["Home network"]
        S["VIRA server<br/>(FastAPI + kernel + agents)"]
        DB[("SQLite WAL<br/>data/vira.sqlite3")]
        FS[("Attachment store<br/>data/attachments/")]
        LLM["LLM (Ollama / optional cloud)"]
        S --- DB
        S --- FS
        S --- LLM
    end

    subgraph Free["Free connectivity (user's choice)"]
        TS["Tailscale (WireGuard mesh)"]
        CF["Cloudflare named tunnel"]
    end

    PG["Push gateway (stateless, content-free)"]
    FCM["FCM / APNs"]

    A1 -- "LAN (mDNS + pinned TLS)" --> S
    A1 -. "VPN / tunnel" .-> TS
    A1 -. "tunnel" .-> CF
    TS --> S
    CF --> S
    S -- "wake-up (opaque handle)" --> PG
    PG --> FCM
    FCM -- "silent push" --> A1

Key ideas

  1. The client is a replica, not a thin UI. The server is the authority (it assigns versions, enforces permissions, decides conflicts).
  2. The only component that a project maintainer operates is the push gateway (stateless, free-tier). Everything else is owned by the family.
  3. Content never goes through the push gateway or through FCM/APNs.

docs.title: 4.5 Key runtime flows
docs.text:
Write path (local-first)

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant UI as UI / Notifier
    participant R as Repository
    participant DB as Local DB
    participant O as Outbox
    participant S as SyncEngine
    participant API as Server

    U->>UI: Edit note
    UI->>R: updateNote(id, patch)
    R->>DB: BEGIN TX, update note (sync_state=pending)
    R->>O: insert op(op_id, upsert, base_version)
    R->>DB: COMMIT
    R-->>UI: Stream emits updated note (instant)
    R->>S: requestSync(reason=localChange)
    S->>API: POST /sync/push {ops}
    API-->>S: results (applied / conflict / duplicate)
    S->>DB: mark synced, store new version

Remote change path

sequenceDiagram
    participant Other as Other member
    participant API as Server
    participant PG as Push gateway
    participant App as This app
    participant S as SyncEngine

    Other->>API: POST /sync/push
    API->>API: append sync_changes (seq N)
    API-->>App: SSE sync.changed {latest_seq}
    API-->>PG: wake-up (if app not connected)
    PG-->>App: silent push
    App->>S: requestSync(reason=hint)
    S->>API: GET /sync/changes?cursor=N-1
    API-->>S: changes[]
    S->>S: apply in one transaction, schedule reminders, raise notifications

docs.title: 4.6 Connectivity architecture
docs.text:
The client keeps an ordered endpoint list (from the pairing QR, editable in settings):

[
  {"kind": "lan",       "url": "https://192.168.1.20:8443", "priority": 10},
  {"kind": "tailscale", "url": "https://vira-home.tail1234.ts.net", "priority": 20},
  {"kind": "tunnel",    "url": "https://vira.example.com", "priority": 30}
]

TransportManager probes GET /health on each (parallel, 1.5 s timeout), picks the lowest-priority-number reachable endpoint, keeps it until it fails or the network changes, and re-probes on connectivity change. All HTTP clients obtain their base URL from the manager; no feature code knows about endpoints.

Path Cost to family When to use Notes LAN Free At home mDNS + pinned self-signed cert Tailscale Free personal plan (non-commercial; check current user limit) Away from home Each member installs the Tailscale app; HTTPS via tailscale serve Cloudflare named tunnel Free service; needs a domain on Cloudflare DNS Away from home, no extra app Quick tunnels (trycloudflare.com) lack SSE and have rotating URLs, so use them for demos only Long-poll fallback Free Any proxy that breaks SSE GET /api/v1/sync/wait

The honest limit: truly zero-config remote access needs a relay someone pays for. v1 deliberately avoids that; a hosted relay can later be added as another kind without client changes.

docs.title: 4.7 Notification architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Local["On device (free, offline)"]
        R1[Reminder rows] --> SCH[Reminder scheduler] --> LN[Local notifications]
    end
    subgraph Remote["Server-originated"]
        EV[Server event e.g. item assigned] --> NS[Notification service]
        NS --> PGW[Push gateway]
        PGW --> FCMX[FCM / APNs]
        FCMX --> WAKE[Silent wake-up in app]
        WAKE --> SYNCX[Sync] --> BUILD[Build visible notification locally]
    end
  • Reminders never depend on push. They are scheduled locally from synced reminder rows.
  • Wake-up payload is { "t": "sync" } plus a collapse key. No titles, names or content.
  • The push gateway stores only push_handle → (provider, token); it never sees user IDs or household data (API in §7.8).

docs.title: 4.9 Architectural decisions (ADR summary)
docs.text: # Decision Rationale Consequence ADR-1 Local-first replica with outbox + cursor sync Offline, instant UI, tolerates a home server that is off Need conflict policy and versioning ADR-2 Sync is the only write path for notes/lists/reminders (attachment creation is the one REST exception, §7.6) One code path to test; idempotent Web client uses the same path ADR-3 Server assigns entity version and change seq No client-clock trust Clients must send base_version ADR-4 Checklist items are separate rows Avoids conflicts inside lists More rows, more ops ADR-5 Note body conflicts keep both versions (conflict copy) Never lose text; no CRDT complexity Occasional manual merge ADR-6 Reminders scheduled locally Offline, free, reliable iOS 64-notification cap handled with a rolling window ADR-7 Content-free push via a shared gateway Each family cannot own a Firebase project One small shared service to run ADR-8 Device credential → short-lived access token Existing credentials have too-narrow scopes; limits blast radius New token endpoints ADR-9 Transport abstraction with ordered endpoints Free paths differ per family Probing logic and diagnostics UI ADR-10 Riverpod + repository interfaces in domain/ Testability Slightly more boilerplate

docs.title: 5.5 State machines
docs.text:
Device pairing

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unpaired
    Unpaired --> Scanning: tap Join
    Scanning --> Validating: QR/code read
    Validating --> Redeeming: endpoint + fingerprint OK
    Validating --> Unpaired: invalid / expired
    Redeeming --> Bootstrapping: credential + tokens stored
    Redeeming --> Unpaired: code used / rejected
    Bootstrapping --> Ready: first sync complete
    Ready --> Locked: device revoked / user disabled
    Locked --> Unpaired: wipe confirmed

Outbox operation

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Queued
    Queued --> InFlight: batch selected
    InFlight --> Done: applied / duplicate
    InFlight --> Queued: network error (backoff)
    InFlight --> Conflict: base_version mismatch
    InFlight --> Failed: rejected (validation / permission)
    Conflict --> Done: conflict copy created
    Failed --> [*]: user dismisses or edits
    Done --> [*]

Note lifecycle: active → archived ↔ active, active → trashed (deleted_at set) → purged after 30 d (server job) or → active (restore).

docs.title: 6.1 Server schema [NEW] (SQLite, WAL; add as a versioned migration in auth/migrations.py)
docs.text:
-- ===== Households ==========================================================
CREATE TABLE households (
  id                 TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                 -- UUIDv7
  name               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(name) BETWEEN 1 AND 60),
  created_by_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  created_at         TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at         TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at         TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE household_members (
  household_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES households(id),
  user_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  role         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin','adult','child','guest')),
  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','removed')),
  display_name TEXT,
  joined_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  removed_at   TEXT,
  version      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  PRIMARY KEY (household_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_members_user ON household_members(user_id, status);

CREATE TABLE pairing_codes (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES households(id),
  created_by    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin','adult','child','guest')),
  code_hash     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,                  -- SHA-256 of the code; raw code shown once
  expires_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  used_at       TEXT,
  used_by_user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id),
  used_device_id  TEXT,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- ===== Tokens for mobile/desktop clients ===================================
CREATE TABLE client_tokens (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- devices.id
  user_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('access','refresh')),
  token_hash    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  scopes        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- space-separated
  expires_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  revoked_at    TEXT,
  rotated_from  TEXT,                                  -- refresh-token reuse detection
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_tokens_device ON client_tokens(device_id, kind, revoked_at);

-- ===== Content =============================================================
CREATE TABLE notebooks (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES households(id),
  owner_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  title         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(title) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  color         TEXT,
  visibility    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'household'
                CHECK (visibility IN ('private','household','custom')),
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at    TEXT,
  updated_by_user_id   INTEGER,
  updated_by_device_id TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notebooks_household ON notebooks(household_id, deleted_at);

CREATE TABLE notebook_shares (
  notebook_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES notebooks(id),
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  permission  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (permission IN ('view','edit')),
  version     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at  TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (notebook_id, user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE notes (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES households(id),
  notebook_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES notebooks(id),
  author_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'note' CHECK (kind IN ('note','checklist')),
  title         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK (length(title) <= 200),
  body_md       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' CHECK (length(body_md) <= 102400),
  pinned        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  archived      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  color         TEXT,
  tags_json     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at    TEXT,
  updated_by_user_id   INTEGER,
  updated_by_device_id TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notes_notebook ON notes(notebook_id, deleted_at, pinned DESC, updated_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE checklist_items (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  note_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES notes(id),
  text          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(text) <= 500),
  done          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  done_by_user_id INTEGER,
  done_at       TEXT,
  position      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- fractional index, e.g. 'a0', 'a0V'
  assignee_user_id INTEGER,
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at    TEXT,
  updated_by_user_id   INTEGER,
  updated_by_device_id TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_items_note ON checklist_items(note_id, deleted_at, position);

CREATE TABLE reminders (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES households(id),
  created_by_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  assignee_user_id   INTEGER,                          -- NULL = everyone
  title         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(title) BETWEEN 1 AND 200),
  body          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  due_at        TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- UTC of first occurrence
  timezone      TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- IANA, e.g. 'Asia/Kolkata'
  rrule         TEXT,                                  -- RFC 5545, e.g. 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO'
  urgent        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  note_id       TEXT,
  item_id       TEXT,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','done','cancelled')),
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at    TEXT,
  updated_by_user_id   INTEGER,
  updated_by_device_id TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_reminders_household ON reminders(household_id, status, due_at);

CREATE TABLE reminder_completions (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  reminder_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES reminders(id),
  user_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  occurrence_at TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- which occurrence was completed
  completed_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  deleted_at    TEXT,
  UNIQUE (reminder_id, user_id, occurrence_at)
);

CREATE TABLE attachments (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  household_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  note_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES notes(id),
  owner_user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  filename      TEXT NOT NULL,
  mime          TEXT NOT NULL,
  size_bytes    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sha256        TEXT NOT NULL,
  storage_path  TEXT,                                  -- relative to data/attachments/
  thumb_path    TEXT,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','ready','failed')),
  uploaded_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  version       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
  deleted_at    TEXT
);

-- ===== Sync ================================================================
CREATE TABLE sync_changes (
  seq            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,    -- the cursor
  household_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_type    TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  notebook_id    TEXT,                                 -- for per-user visibility filtering
  op             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (op IN ('upsert','delete','forget')),
  version        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  target_user_id INTEGER,                               -- set only for 'forget' (deliver to one user)
  actor_user_id  INTEGER,
  actor_device_id TEXT,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_changes_household_seq ON sync_changes(household_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX idx_changes_entity ON sync_changes(entity_type, entity_id, seq);

CREATE TABLE sync_op_receipts (                         -- idempotency for POST /sync/push
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL,
  op_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  status     TEXT NOT NULL,                              -- applied | conflict | rejected
  result_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (device_id, op_id)
);

-- ===== Push / notifications ================================================
CREATE TABLE push_registrations (
  id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  provider    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (provider IN ('fcm','unifiedpush','ntfy')),
  push_handle TEXT NOT NULL,                             -- opaque handle issued by push gateway (or UP endpoint)
  locale      TEXT,
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  revoked_at  TEXT,
  UNIQUE (device_id, provider)
);

CREATE TABLE notification_prefs (
  user_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
  household_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  category     TEXT NOT NULL,
  enabled      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  quiet_start  TEXT,                                     -- 'HH:MM' local
  quiet_end    TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, household_id, category)
);

Per-user visibility rule for pull (server-side)

A change row is delivered to user U if any of:

  1. entity_type IN ('household','member') and U is an active member;
  2. its notebook_id is visible to U: notebook visibility='household' and U is an active member, or U owns it, or a non-deleted notebook_shares row exists for U;
  3. op='forget' and target_user_id = U;
  4. entity_type='reminder' / 'reminder_completion' and (assignee_user_id IS NULL or = U or U created it).

Guests only receive notebooks explicitly shared with them. Children never receive private notebooks of others (this is already covered by rule 2).

docs.title: 6.2 Client local schema (drift / SQLite)
docs.text:
Timestamps are epoch milliseconds. Every synced table has sync_state and base_version columns used by the outbox logic.

CREATE TABLE households (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, my_role TEXT NOT NULL,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE members (
  household_id TEXT NOT NULL, user_id TEXT NOT NULL,       -- user public_id
  display_name TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (household_id, user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE notebooks (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, owner_user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL, color TEXT, visibility TEXT NOT NULL,
  my_permission TEXT NOT NULL,                              -- 'edit' | 'view' (computed on apply)
  version INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  deleted_at INTEGER, sync_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'synced'
);

CREATE TABLE notebook_shares (
  notebook_id TEXT NOT NULL, user_id TEXT NOT NULL, permission TEXT NOT NULL,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL, deleted_at INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (notebook_id, user_id)
);

CREATE TABLE notes (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, notebook_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  author_user_id TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL, body_md TEXT NOT NULL,
  pinned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, archived INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  color TEXT, tags_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,                       -- 0 = never synced
  base_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,                  -- version the local edit started from
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, deleted_at INTEGER,
  updated_by_user_id TEXT, updated_by_device_id TEXT,
  conflict_of TEXT,                                         -- id of original when this is a conflict copy
  sync_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'synced'
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notes_list ON notes(notebook_id, deleted_at, archived, pinned DESC, updated_at DESC);

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE notes_fts USING fts5(title, body_md, content='notes', content_rowid='rowid');
-- triggers keep notes_fts in sync with notes (insert/update/delete), excluding deleted rows

CREATE TABLE checklist_items (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, note_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  text TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, done_by_user_id TEXT, done_at INTEGER,
  position TEXT NOT NULL, assignee_user_id TEXT,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, base_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, deleted_at INTEGER,
  sync_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'synced'
);
CREATE INDEX idx_items_note ON checklist_items(note_id, deleted_at, position);

CREATE TABLE reminders (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, created_by_user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  assignee_user_id TEXT, title TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  due_at INTEGER NOT NULL, timezone TEXT NOT NULL, rrule TEXT, urgent INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  note_id TEXT, item_id TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, base_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, deleted_at INTEGER, sync_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'synced'
);
CREATE INDEX idx_reminders_due ON reminders(household_id, status, due_at);

CREATE TABLE reminder_completions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, reminder_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  user_id TEXT NOT NULL, occurrence_at INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, deleted_at INTEGER, sync_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'synced',
  UNIQUE (reminder_id, user_id, occurrence_at)
);

CREATE TABLE scheduled_notifications (                      -- what the OS currently has scheduled
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,                                   -- OS notification id
  reminder_id TEXT NOT NULL, occurrence_at INTEGER NOT NULL, fire_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE attachments (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, household_id TEXT NOT NULL, note_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  filename TEXT NOT NULL, mime TEXT NOT NULL, size_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL, sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
  local_path TEXT, thumb_path TEXT,
  transfer_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'remote_only',       -- remote_only|downloading|cached|upload_pending|uploading|failed
  transferred_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_access_at INTEGER,
  version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, deleted_at INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE outbox (
  op_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                                   -- UUIDv7, also the idempotency key
  seq INTEGER NOT NULL,                                     -- local ordering (autoincrement via separate counter)
  household_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_type TEXT NOT NULL, entity_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  op TEXT NOT NULL,                                         -- upsert | delete
  base_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payload_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued',                    -- queued|in_flight|failed
  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, next_attempt_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_ready ON outbox(status, next_attempt_at, seq);

CREATE TABLE sync_state (                                   -- key/value
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL                 -- 'cursor:<household_id>', 'last_full_sync', ...
);

CREATE TABLE conversations (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, household_id TEXT, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE messages (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL,
  content TEXT NOT NULL, sequence_no INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sent'                        -- draft|sending|sent|failed
);
CREATE INDEX idx_messages_conv ON messages(conversation_id, sequence_no);

CREATE TABLE endpoints (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, url TEXT NOT NULL, priority INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_ok_at INTEGER, last_latency_ms INTEGER, last_error TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE app_settings (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);

Secrets are never in this DB. Access/refresh tokens, the device credential and the SQLCipher key live in OS secure storage (§9.5).

docs.title: 6.3 Migration policy
docs.text:
• Server: add as the next numbered migration; migrations are idempotent and recorded in schema_migrations (existing mechanism).
  • Client: drift schemaVersion with MigrationStrategy.stepByStep; before any migration, copy the DB file to vira.db.bak-<version>; keep the last backup until the next successful launch (CNFR-20).
  • A change to an API payload is additive within a protocol version; breaking changes bump proto (CNFR-14).

docs.title: 7.1 Conventions
docs.text: Topic Rule Base path /api/v1 Format JSON (application/json; charset=utf-8), except chat stream (application/x-ndjson) and attachment bytes Auth Authorization: Bearer <access_token> for the Flutter clients on mobile/desktop. Flutter web uses the existing session cookie (vira_session) from POST /api/v1/auth/login. Client header X-Vira-Client: flutter/1.0.0 proto/1 on every request Correlation Client sends X-Correlation-ID (UUID); server echoes it (existing behaviour) Idempotency Mutating non-sync endpoints accept Idempotency-Key; sync ops use op_id Pagination Cursor style: ?limit=50&cursor=<opaque> → { "items": [...], "next_cursor": "..." \| null } (existing convention) Time UTC ISO-8601 (2026-11-04T10:15:30Z) Errors { "detail": "...", "error": { "code": "sync.cursor_expired", "message": "...", "correlation_id": "..." } } Compression Accept-Encoding: gzip supported on all JSON responses Limits See CNFR-15 and GET /client-config

docs.title: 7.2.1 QR payload (what the admin's screen shows)
docs.text:
Encoded as vira://pair?d=<base64url(JSON)>:

{
  "v": 1,
  "server_id": "srv_01JC3R8...",
  "name": "Sharma Family",
  "household_id": "0192f6b2-7c1e-7a55-9d3a-5f1c0d6e8a11",
  "code": "7QK4M9XB",
  "endpoints": [
    { "kind": "lan",       "url": "https://192.168.1.20:8443",          "priority": 10 },
    { "kind": "tailscale", "url": "https://vira-home.tail1234.ts.net", "priority": 20 }

The app must refuse the payload if v is unknown, code is empty, or no endpoint is reachable and matches cert_sha256 (for self-signed LAN certs) or a valid public certificate (for tunnel/Tailscale HTTPS).

Requires an authenticated household admin (to add a member) or the user themself (to add another device).

Request

  "household_id": "0192f6b2-...",

Response 201

Request

  "user": { "display_name": "Anita" },            // required for join_household, ignored for add_device
  "device": {

}
Response 201 
{
  "server": { "id": "srv_01JC3R8...", "name": "Sharma Family", "protocol": 1, "time": "2026-11-04T10:16:02Z" },
  "user": { "public_id": "usr_8f2a...", "display_name": "Anita", "platform_role": "member" },
  "household": { "id": "0192f6b2-...", "name": "Sharma Family", "role": "adult" },
  "device": { "id": "dev_5c21...", "display_name": "Anita's Pixel 8" },
  "device_credential": { "credential_id": "cred_77...", "token": "vdc_live_...", "expires_at": "2027-11-04T10:16:02Z" },

docs.title: 7.2.4 POST /api/v1/auth/token [NEW] — refresh / re-authenticate
docs.text:
{ "grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": "vrt_..." }
or, if the refresh token was lost or expired: 
{ "grant_type": "device_credential", "device_id": "dev_5c21...", "credential": "vdc_live_..." }
Response 200: same tokens object as above. Refresh tokens rotate: the old one is revoked and linked via rotated_from. Presenting an already-rotated refresh token is treated as theft: the whole token family for that device is revoked and the response is 401 auth.token_reuse.

Scopes granted: sync:read sync:write chat attachments devices:self households:read, plus households:admin when the user is a household admin.

Method & path Purpose Who GET /households List my households any member POST /households { "name": "..." } Create; caller becomes admin any non-guest user GET /households/{id} Details + my_role member PATCH /households/{id} { "name": "..." } Rename admin GET /households/{id}/members List members (also delivered through sync as member entities) member PATCH /households/{id}/members/{user_public_id} { "role": "child" } Change role admin DELETE /households/{id}/members/{user_public_id} Remove member (server emits forget changes for that user) admin DELETE /households/{id}/members/me Leave member (not last admin)

docs.title: 7.5 Sync API [NEW] (the only write path for notes, lists, reminders)
7.5.1 GET /api/v1/sync/changes
docs.text:
Query: household_id (required), cursor (integer, default 0), limit (≤ 500).

cursor=0 is a bootstrap: the server returns the user's visible state as synthetic upsert changes in dependency order (households → members → notebooks → shares → notes → items → reminders → completions → attachments) with "snapshot": true and a snapshot_seq the client then uses as its cursor.

Response 200 

{
  "household_id": "0192f6b2-...",
  "snapshot": false,
  "changes": [
    {
      "seq": 1042,
      "entity_type": "note",
      "entity_id": "0192f6d1-...",
      "op": "upsert",
      "version": 4,
      "actor": { "user_id": "usr_8f2a...", "device_id": "dev_5c21..." },
      "changed_at": "2026-11-04T10:15:30Z",
      "data": {
        "id": "0192f6d1-...", "household_id": "0192f6b2-...", "notebook_id": "0192f6c4-...",
        "kind": "note", "title": "Electricity bill", "body_md": "Due **12 Nov**. Paid via UPI.",
        "pinned": true, "archived": false, "color": null, "tags": ["bills"],
        "author_user_id": "usr_8f2a...",
        "created_at": "2026-11-01T08:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-11-04T10:15:30Z", "deleted_at": null
      }
    },
    {
      "seq": 1043, "entity_type": "checklist_item", "entity_id": "0192f6d9-...", "op": "delete", "version": 3,
      "actor": { "user_id": "usr_1b7e...", "device_id": "dev_a901..." }, "changed_at": "2026-11-04T10:15:31Z",
      "data": { "id": "0192f6d9-...", "note_id": "0192f6d2-...", "deleted_at": "2026-11-04T10:15:31Z" }
    },
    {
      "seq": 1044, "entity_type": "notebook", "entity_id": "0192f6c9-...", "op": "forget", "version": 0,
      "actor": null, "changed_at": "2026-11-04T10:16:00Z", "data": null
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": 1044,
  "has_more": false,
  "server_time": "2026-11-04T10:16:05Z"
}

Rules: - op=upsert → insert or replace the local row if version is greater than the local version. - op=delete → set deleted_at (tombstone); client hides the row. - op=forget → physically remove the entity and all its children from the local DB (access lost). Never shown as a deletion in the UI. - Changes are ordered by seq; the client must apply a page in one transaction and persist next_cursor in the same transaction. - 410 Gone with error.code = "sync.cursor_expired" means the cursor is older than the compaction floor; the client discards local synced data for that household (keeping un-pushed outbox ops) and bootstraps with cursor=0.

docs.title: 7.5.2 POST /api/v1/sync/push
docs.text:
Request 

{
  "device_id": "dev_5c21...",
  "household_id": "0192f6b2-...",
  "ops": [
    {
      "op_id": "0192f700-0a1b-7c3d-8e9f-001122334455",
      "entity_type": "note",
      "entity_id": "0192f6d1-...",
      "op": "upsert",
      "base_version": 4,
      "fields": ["body_md"],
      "data": { "id": "0192f6d1-...", "notebook_id": "0192f6c4-...", "kind": "note",
                "title": "Electricity bill", "body_md": "Due **12 Nov**. Paid via UPI & cash." }
    },
    {
      "op_id": "0192f700-0a1c-7a11-8e9f-001122334456",
      "entity_type": "checklist_item",
      "entity_id": "0192f6da-...",
      "op": "upsert",
      "base_version": 0,
      "data": { "id": "0192f6da-...", "note_id": "0192f6d2-...", "text": "Milk 2L", "done": false,
                "position": "a0V", "assignee_user_id": null }
    }
  ]
}
- base_version: the entity version the edit started from (0 for a new entity). - fields: optional list of changed fields, used for field-level merge (see 7.5.4). - Max 200 ops / 1 MB per request; ops are applied in order and each in its own savepoint, so one rejected op never blocks the others.

Response 200 

{
  "results": [
    { "op_id": "0192f700-0a1b-...", "status": "applied",   "version": 5 },
    { "op_id": "0192f700-0a1c-...", "status": "duplicate", "version": 1 },
    { "op_id": "0192f700-0a1d-...", "status": "conflict", "reason": "version_mismatch",
      "server": { "version": 7, "data": { "...": "current server entity" } } },
    { "op_id": "0192f700-0a1e-...", "status": "rejected",
      "error": { "code": "household.permission_denied", "message": "Notebook is view-only for you." } }
  ],
  "latest_seq": 1051
}
status values: applied, duplicate (same op_id already processed → return stored result), conflict, rejected.

docs.title: 7.5.3 Idempotency and ordering guarantees
docs.text:
• Server stores (device_id, op_id) → result in sync_op_receipts in the same transaction as the entity change and the sync_changes row.
  • The client keeps an op in the outbox until it receives a terminal status. Retrying after a timeout is therefore always safe.
  • Ordering inside one client is preserved by outbox.seq; across clients the server's seq defines the order.

docs.title: 7.5.4 Conflict policy per entity
docs.text: Entity Stale base_version handling note — title, body_md Conflict. Server keeps its version; returns conflict + current server data. Client creates a conflict copy (§8.6). note — only pinned, archived, color, tags in fields Merged, last-writer-wins by arrival time; applied. checklist_item Last-writer-wins per item (applied); toggling done and editing text by different people merge field-wise using fields. reminder Last-writer-wins; assignee changes always win over completion. reminder_completion Unique on (reminder, user, occurrence); re-sending is duplicate. notebook, notebook_share Owner/admin LWW; non-owners get rejected. Edit vs deleted entity Delete wins: conflict with reason: "deleted"; client keeps its text as a conflict copy when it was a note.

docs.title: 7.5.5 GET /api/v1/sync/wait — long-poll fallback
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/sync/wait?household_id=...&cursor=1044&timeout=25

Returns 200 { "latest_seq": 1051, "changed": true } as soon as latest_seq > cursor, or { "changed": false } after timeout seconds (max 30). Used when SSE is unavailable (CFR-97).

docs.title: 7.6 Attachments [NEW] (v2)
docs.text:
Attachment metadata is created over REST (the server must allocate storage); deletion and later metadata changes still go through sync.

Step Request Response 1. Create POST /attachments { "id": "<uuidv7>", "note_id": "...", "filename": "bill.jpg", "mime": "image/jpeg", "size_bytes": 482113, "sha256": "ab12..." } 201 { "id": "...", "status": "pending", "upload": { "url": "/api/v1/attachments/{id}/content", "chunk_size": 1048576 } } 2. Resume check HEAD /attachments/{id}/content 200 + header Upload-Offset: 0 3. Upload chunk PATCH /attachments/{id}/content headers Upload-Offset: N, Content-Type: application/offset+octet-stream, body = bytes 204 + Upload-Offset: N+len 4. Completion Automatic when Upload-Offset == size_bytes; server verifies SHA-256, sets status=ready, emits a sync change — Download GET /attachments/{id}/content (supports Range) bytes Thumbnail GET /attachments/{id}/thumbnail image/jpeg ≤ 20 KB

Errors: limits.attachment_too_large (413), attachment.hash_mismatch (422).

Event type data Client reaction sync.changed { "household_id": "...", "latest_seq": 1051 } SyncEngine.requestSync(hint) device.revoked { "device_id": "..." } Lock app (CFR-07) session.revoked {} Re-authenticate with device credential or lock kernel.*, sensor.*, agent.* — Ignored by the family client

docs.title: 7.8 Push registration and the push gateway
7.8.1 Client → VIRA server [NEW]
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/devices/{device_id}/push-registration 

{ "provider": "fcm", "push_handle": "ph_9d1c...", "locale": "hi-IN" }
DELETE /api/v1/devices/{device_id}/push-registration?provider=fcm — unregister.

docs.title: 7.8.2 Push gateway (separate tiny service) [NEW]
docs.text:
The gateway exists only because each family cannot own a Firebase project. It maps opaque handles to provider tokens and forwards content-free wake-ups.

Endpoint Caller Body → Response POST /v1/servers VIRA server (once) { "server_name": "optional", "version": "0.9.0" } → { "server_id": "srv_...", "server_secret": "..." } POST /v1/handles Flutter app { "server_id": "srv_...", "provider": "fcm", "token": "<fcm token>", "platform": "android" } → { "push_handle": "ph_9d1c..." } POST /v1/push VIRA server Headers X-Server-Id, X-Timestamp, X-Signature: HMAC-SHA256(server_secret, timestamp + "." + body); body { "handles": ["ph_9d1c..."], "collapse_key": "sync", "priority": "high" } → { "accepted": 1, "invalid_handles": [] } DELETE /v1/handles/{push_handle} Flutter app 204

Rules: payload delivered to the device is always { "t": "sync" } (plus the collapse key); the gateway rejects any other field. A handle is valid only for the server_id it was created with. The server removes handles listed in invalid_handles. Rate limits: 30 pushes/min per handle, 600/min per server.

docs.title: 7.9 Error codes
docs.text: HTTP error.code Meaning / client action 400 validation_error Show field errors; do not retry 401 auth.invalid_token / auth.token_expired Refresh once, then re-auth 401 auth.token_reuse Lock + force re-pair 403 household.permission_denied Show message; mark op failed 403 auth.device_revoked / auth.user_disabled Lock app (CFR-07) 404 pairing.invalid_code, not_found Show message 409 pairing.used, sync.version_conflict Conflict flow 410 pairing.expired, sync.cursor_expired Re-pair / re-bootstrap 413 limits.note_too_large, limits.attachment_too_large Block in UI 426 protocol.upgrade_required "Update the app" screen 429 rate_limited Honour Retry-After 5xx server_error Backoff and retry

docs.title: 7.10 Server work packages (summary)
8.1 Project structure and layering rules
docs.text:
Feature-first, layered. One Dart package (vira_family); split into packages later only if build times demand it.

vira_family/
├─ lib/
│  ├─ main.dart                      # bootstrap: ProviderScope, error zone, DB + secure-store init
│  ├─ app/
│  │  ├─ app.dart                    # MaterialApp.router, theme, l10n delegates
│  │  ├─ router.dart                 # go_router config, auth/pairing redirect guards, deep links
│  │  ├─ theme/                      # ColorScheme, text styles, dark theme
│  │  └─ l10n/                       # app_en.arb, app_hi.arb
│  ├─ core/
│  │  ├─ clock.dart                  # abstract Clock + SystemClock + ServerClock (offset)
│  │  ├─ ids.dart                    # Uuid7 generator (injectable)
│  │  ├─ result.dart                 # Result<T, AppFailure>
│  │  ├─ failures.dart               # sealed AppFailure hierarchy
│  │  ├─ logging/                    # redacting logger, ring buffer, export
│  │  └─ platform/                   # capability flags (isWeb, supportsMdns, supportsBgTasks)
│  ├─ domain/
│  │  ├─ entities/                   # Household, Member, Notebook, Note, ChecklistItem, Reminder, ...
│  │  ├─ repositories/               # abstract interfaces (NotesRepository, ...)
│  │  └─ usecases/                   # CreateNote, ToggleItem, CompleteReminder, ...
│  ├─ data/
│  │  ├─ local/
│  │  │  ├─ app_database.dart        # drift @DriftDatabase, migrations
│  │  │  ├─ tables/                  # one file per table (§6.2)
│  │  │  └─ daos/                    # NotesDao, OutboxDao, SyncStateDao, ...
│  │  ├─ remote/
│  │  │  ├─ transport_manager.dart   # endpoint selection, probing, pinning
│  │  │  ├─ api_client.dart          # dio instance, interceptors
│  │  │  ├─ dto/                     # freezed JSON DTOs matching §7
│  │  │  └─ services/                # AuthApi, SyncApi, HouseholdApi, ChatApi, PushApi
│  │  ├─ sync/
│  │  │  ├─ sync_engine.dart
│  │  │  ├─ outbox.dart
│  │  │  ├─ change_applier.dart      # per-entity apply of pulled changes
│  │  │  └─ conflict_resolver.dart
│  │  ├─ secure/secure_store.dart    # tokens, credential, db key
│  │  └─ repositories/               # *_repository_impl.dart
│  ├─ platform_services/
│  │  ├─ notifications/              # notification_service.dart, reminder_scheduler.dart, policy.dart
│  │  ├─ push/                       # push_provider.dart (interface), fcm_provider.dart
│  │  ├─ background/                 # workmanager callbacks
│  │  ├─ share/share_receiver.dart
│  │  ├─ discovery/mdns_discovery.dart
│  │  └─ speech/speech_service.dart
│  └─ features/
│     ├─ onboarding/  ├─ pairing/  ├─ notes/  ├─ lists/  ├─ reminders/
│     ├─ household/   ├─ chat/     ├─ search/ ├─ settings/ (privacy, devices, connection, notifications)
│     └─ <feature>/{presentation (screens, widgets), application (notifiers/controllers)}
├─ test/                             # unit + widget tests mirroring lib/
├─ integration_test/
├─ android/ ios/ linux/ web/
└─ pubspec.yaml, analysis_options.yaml, l10n.yaml

Rules (enforced with import_lint/custom lint in CI)

  1. domain/ imports only dart:core and pure-Dart packages (freezed_annotation, rrule, meta).
  2. features/*/presentation talks only to features/*/application and domain/.
  3. features/A never imports features/B/presentation. Shared widgets go to app/widgets/.
  4. Only data/ and platform_services/ may import dio, drift, firebase_*, flutter_local_notifications.
  5. Every side-effecting dependency (clock, ids, http, db, notifications) is injected through a Riverpod provider so tests can override it.
